subject: math
title: Grade 5 Prisms and Pyramids
seo_title: Grade 5 Prisms and Pyramids Worksheets: Faces, Edges, Vertices and Nets (Free, BC Curriculum, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on prisms and pyramids for the BC curriculum: tell a prism from a pyramid, name each one by its base, count faces, edges and vertices, match nets, and solve problems with tents, boxes and straw frames. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point.
key_sub: Name both by the shape of the base: 2 triangle bases make a triangular prism, and a square base with 4 triangles makes a square pyramid. Do not name an object by the face it sits on or by its number of faces.
body_html:
Prism or pyramid?

A prism has 2 matching bases that face each other. Rectangles join them.

A pyramid has 1 base. Its other faces are triangles that meet at one point, the apex.

Name it by its base

Look at the base and count its sides. That shape gives the name: a triangle base makes a triangular prism or pyramid.

Example 1

An object has 2 matching pentagons joined by 5 rectangles. What is it?

2 matching bases joined by rectangles: a prism. The bases have 5 sides: pentagons.

Answer: a pentagonal prism

Example 2

An object has 1 square and 4 triangles that meet at a point. What is it?

1 base and triangles: a pyramid. The base is a square.

Answer: a square pyramid

Faces, edges and vertices

A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

ObjectFacesEdgesVertices
Triangular prism596
Rectangular prism6128
Pentagonal prism71510
Hexagonal prism81812
Triangular pyramid464
Square pyramid585
Pentagonal pyramid6106
Hexagonal pyramid7127
Example 3

How many edges does a hexagonal pyramid have?

6 edges round the base + 6 edges up to the apex: 6 + 6.

Answer: 12 edges

Nets

A net is a flat pattern that folds up into the object. A prism’s net has 2 bases and a rectangle for each side of the base. A pyramid’s net has 1 base and a triangle on each side of it.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a triangular prism a pyramid because it has trianglesCount the bases: 2 matching bases means a prism
Naming a prism by the face it sits on or by a side faceFind the 2 matching ends: they are the bases
Naming by the number of faces (a triangular prism has 5 faces, but it is not “pentagonal”)Count the sides of the base
Counting only the faces you can seeCount the hidden faces at the back and the bottom too
Forgetting the apex when counting a pyramid’s verticesVertices = the corners of the base + 1
Calling a cylinder a “circular prism”A cylinder has a curved surface, so it is not a prism

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about prisms and pyramids in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 5 math curriculum includes the classification of prisms and pyramids. Students tell prisms from pyramids, name them by their base, count faces, edges and vertices, and match them to their nets.

faq.q: How do you name a prism or a pyramid?
faq.a: Use the shape of the base. A prism with triangle bases is a triangular prism, and a pyramid with a square base is a square pyramid. Do not use the side faces or the number of faces.

faq.q: What is the difference between a prism and a pyramid?
faq.a: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. A pyramid has 1 base, and its other faces are triangles that meet at a point called the apex.

faq.q: How many faces, edges and vertices does a square pyramid have?
faq.a: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. A triangular prism also has 5 faces, but it has 9 edges and 6 vertices.

items.q: What kind of object is this?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The square is the base, and 4 triangles meet at the top.

items.q: How many bases does a square pyramid have?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The square is the only base. The 4 triangles are side faces, and 5 is the number of faces in all.

items.q: In a pyramid, what shape are the faces that are not the base?
c: the same shape as the base
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). Rectangles join the bases of a prism.
It has 2 matching circles and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A prism has only flat faces, so a cylinder is not a prism.

items.q: How many bases does a prism have?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. 1 base belongs to a pyramid.

items.q: Which word describes this object?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The base has 5 sides, and 5 triangles meet at the top.

items.q: Is this object a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. The 2 triangle ends match, and 3 rectangles join them. Triangle faces do not always mean a pyramid.

items.q: Is this object a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. Every face is a rectangle. Any two opposite faces can be the bases.

items.q: Simran says, “This object has triangle faces, so it must be a pyramid.” The object has 2 matching triangles joined by 3 rectangles. Is she right?
c: Yes, triangles always make a pyramid
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. This object is a triangular prism. A pyramid has only 1 base, and its triangles meet at a point.

items.q: Which object is a pyramid?
items.e: B has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point. The other objects have 2 matching bases joined by rectangles, so they are prisms.

items.q: What kind of object is this?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. The front and back are matching shapes with 5 sides, joined by rectangles. The pointed roof does not make it a pyramid.

items.q: Why is this object a pyramid?
c: It has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles
It has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point
items.e: The hexagon is the base, and 6 triangles meet at the apex. Having triangle faces is not enough: a triangular prism has triangles too.

items.q: An object has 1 hexagon face and 6 triangle faces that meet at a point. What kind of object is it?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The hexagon is the base, so it is a hexagonal pyramid.

items.q: Is this object a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). All 4 faces are triangles, and 3 of them meet at the top.

items.q: Which object has an apex?
items.e: Only a pyramid has triangles that meet at one point. The prisms have 2 bases and no apex.
A has 2 matching pentagon bases joined by rectangles. The others come to a point: two pyramids and a cone.

items.q: Which word describes this object?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. The top and bottom are matching hexagons, joined by 6 rectangles.

items.q: Why is this object a prism?
c: It has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles
It has 1 base and an apex
items.e: The top and bottom are matching triangles, and 3 rectangles join them. A square pyramid also has 5 faces, so that is not the reason.

items.q: In a prism, what shape are the faces that join the two bases?
c: the same shape as the bases
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. Triangles that meet at a point belong to a pyramid.

items.q: The point at the top of a pyramid, where the triangles meet, is called the …
items.e: The apex is the vertex where all the triangle faces meet. The base is the face opposite the apex.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base is a triangle, so it is a triangular pyramid. All 4 faces are triangles. Do not name it by its 4 faces: that would give a 4-sided base.

items.q: A cube is a special kind of which prism?
items.e: A cube has square bases joined by squares, and a square is a special rectangle. So a cube is a rectangular prism. Its 6 faces do not make it “hexagonal”.

items.q: The bases of a prism are hexagons. What is its name?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Hexagon bases make a hexagonal prism. The side faces are rectangles, but they do not name it.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base is a square, so it is a square pyramid. Do not name it by its triangle side faces or by its 5 faces.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Count the sides of an end: 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal prism. 7 is its number of faces.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Each end has 8 sides, so it is an octagonal prism. 10 is its number of faces.

items.q: Which face do you use to name a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. A prism can lie on a rectangle, but its bases are still the 2 matching ends.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Each end has 6 sides, so it is a hexagonal prism. 8 is its number of faces, and the rectangles are only the side faces.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base has 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal pyramid. 6 is its number of faces.

items.q: Which object is a pentagonal prism?
items.e: C has 2 matching pentagon ends joined by rectangles. The others are a hexagonal prism, a pentagonal pyramid and a triangular prism.

items.q: Which object is a square pyramid?
items.e: D has a square base and 4 triangles that meet at a point. The others are a triangular pyramid, a rectangular prism and a pentagonal pyramid.

items.q: An object has 1 rectangle base and 4 triangles that meet at a point. What is its name?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. 1 base and triangles make a pyramid, and the base is a rectangle: a rectangular pyramid.

items.q: A pyramid has a base with 5 sides. What is its name?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. 5 sides make a pentagon, so it is a pentagonal pyramid.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The end looks like a house: a square with a triangle on top. Count its sides: 5. So it is a pentagonal prism, not a triangular prism.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base has 6 sides, so it is a hexagonal pyramid. 7 is its number of faces.

items.q: What shape is each base of a triangular prism?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. A triangular prism has 2 triangle bases. Its 3 side faces are rectangles.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base is a long rectangle, so it is a rectangular pyramid. The triangles are side faces, so they do not name it.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The bases are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism. It has 6 faces, but “hexagonal” would mean hexagon bases. It is not a cube, because its faces are not all squares.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. This prism stands on a base. The top and bottom are matching pentagons, so it is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The 2 matching ends are triangles, so it is a triangular prism. It lies on a rectangle, but that face is not a base. Do not use its 5 faces: that would give “pentagonal”.

items.q: How many vertices does a hexagonal prism have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6).

items.q: Which has more edges, a triangular prism or a square pyramid?
items.e: Triangular prism: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 edges. Square pyramid: 4 round the base + 4 up to the apex = 8 edges. 9 − 8 = 1.

items.q: How many faces does a hexagonal pyramid have?
items.e: A hexagonal pyramid has 7 faces (1 hexagon + 6 triangles), 12 edges (6 round the base + 6 up to the apex) and 7 vertices (6 + 1 apex). 8 would be a hexagonal prism.

items.q: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). 3 edges round each end and 3 joining the ends.

items.q: This is a triangular pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 faces (1 triangle + 3 triangles), 6 edges (3 round the base + 3 up to the apex) and 4 vertices (3 + 1 apex). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). You can see only 3 faces, but the bottom and the back end count too.

items.q: A prism has 12 vertices. What is its name?
items.e: Half the vertices are on each base: 12 ÷ 2 = 6, so the bases are hexagons. (Decagonal uses the faces rule, 12 − 2, and rectangular uses the edges rule, 12 ÷ 3.)

items.q: What is an edge?
c: the face an object sits on
a line where two faces meet
items.e: An edge is a line segment where two faces meet. A corner is a vertex, and a flat surface is a face.

items.q: A pyramid has 6 faces. What is its name?
items.e: Faces of a pyramid = the base + 1 triangle for each side of the base. 6 − 1 = 5 sides, so the base is a pentagon. (Square pyramid uses the prism rule, 6 − 2 = 4.)

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a pentagonal prism have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5).

items.q: How many vertices does a square pyramid have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square + 4 triangles), 8 edges (4 round the base + 4 up to the apex) and 5 vertices (4 + 1 apex). Do not forget the apex.

items.q: How many edges does a square pyramid have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square + 4 triangles), 8 edges (4 round the base + 4 up to the apex) and 5 vertices (4 + 1 apex).

items.q: A triangular prism and a square pyramid both have 5 faces. What else is true?
c: The prism has 6 vertices and the pyramid has 5
They have the same number of vertices
The prism has 5 vertices and the pyramid has 6
items.e: Triangular prism: 9 edges, 6 vertices. Square pyramid: 8 edges, 5 vertices.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3).

items.q: This is a pentagonal pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal pyramid has 6 faces (1 pentagon + 5 triangles), 10 edges (5 round the base + 5 up to the apex) and 6 vertices (5 + 1 apex). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces (2 rectangles + 4 rectangles), 12 edges (4 + 4 + 4) and 8 vertices (4 + 4). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a hexagonal pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal pyramid has 7 faces (1 hexagon + 6 triangles), 12 edges (6 round the base + 6 up to the apex) and 7 vertices (6 + 1 apex).

items.q: This is a square pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square + 4 triangles), 8 edges (4 round the base + 4 up to the apex) and 5 vertices (4 + 1 apex). Do not forget the square base on the bottom.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6). Do not forget the 6 edges that join the two ends.

items.q: Why will this NOT fold into a hexagonal prism?
c: Both hexagons fold onto the same end
items.e: Both hexagons are on the top edge, so they fold onto the same end and the other end stays open. One hexagon must be on the top edge and one on the bottom edge.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There is 1 hexagon and 6 triangles that meet at a point, so it is a hexagonal pyramid.

items.q: A net has 1 hexagon and 6 triangles. Which object does it fold into?
items.e: 1 base and triangles make a pyramid. The base is a hexagon, so it is a hexagonal pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There are 2 hexagons and 6 rectangles. The hexagons are the matching ends, so it is a hexagonal prism.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
c: it cannot fold into an object
items.e: There are 4 matching triangles. One is the base, and the other 3 fold up and meet at a point: a triangular pyramid.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The triangles are the matching ends, so it folds into a triangular prism.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 2 pentagons and 5 rectangles. The pentagons are the matching ends, so it is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: The net of a pyramid has 5 triangles and 1 other shape. What is the other shape?
items.e: There is 1 triangle for each side of the base, so the base has 5 sides: a pentagon. (Hexagon counts all 6 faces.)

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There is 1 square and 4 triangles. The triangles fold up and meet at a point, so it is a square pyramid.

items.q: Kai cuts out a net with 2 triangles and 3 rectangles and says it makes a triangular pyramid. What does it really make?
items.e: 2 matching triangles joined by rectangles make a triangular prism. A triangular pyramid’s net has 4 triangles and no rectangles.

items.q: Which net folds into a square pyramid?
items.e: C has 1 square and 4 triangles. One other net has only 3 triangles, one makes a triangular prism and one makes a pentagonal pyramid.

items.q: How many triangles are in the net of a square pyramid?
items.e: 1 square base + 4 triangles, one on each side of the square. 5 is the number of faces in all.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There is 1 pentagon and 5 triangles that meet at a point, so it is a pentagonal pyramid. 6 is its number of faces.

items.q: This net of a square pyramid is missing one face. Which shape is missing?
items.e: A square pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles. The net has only 3 triangles, so one side of the square has nothing to fold up.

items.q: A net has 2 pentagons and 5 rectangles. Which object does it fold into?
items.e: 2 matching pentagons joined by rectangles make a pentagonal prism. 7 is the number of faces.

items.q: A net has 4 matching triangles and no other shapes. What does it fold into?
c: it cannot fold into an object
items.e: One triangle is the base and the other 3 fold up and meet at a point, so it makes a triangular pyramid.

items.q: How many rectangles are in the net of a hexagonal prism?
items.e: 1 rectangle for each side of the hexagon: 6. With the 2 hexagons there are 8 faces in all.

items.q: This net of a pentagonal prism is missing one face. Which shape is missing?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 2 pentagons and 5 rectangles. The net has all 5 rectangles but only 1 pentagon.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: B has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. One net has only 2 rectangles, so it cannot close up; the others make a triangular pyramid and a square pyramid.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, so it folds into a rectangular prism. It is not a cube, because the faces are not all squares.

sets.title: Real objects: tents, boxes and more

items.q: Mei puts tape along every edge of a cube-shaped gift box. Each edge is 15 cm long. How much tape does she use?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 15 = 180 cm. 90 cm uses the 6 faces, 120 cm the 8 vertices and 60 cm only 4 edges.

items.q: A gazebo in a park has a roof shaped like a hexagonal pyramid with no base. How many triangle panels make the roof?
items.e: A hexagonal pyramid has 1 triangle for each side of the hexagon: 6 triangles. 7 counts the base too, and 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Zara joins straws with balls of modelling clay at every corner of a triangular prism. How many balls of clay does she need?
items.e: One ball for each vertex: 3 on each triangle end, 3 + 3 = 6. 9 is the number of edges.

items.q: Nadia’s family rents an A-frame cabin near Whistler. Its front and back walls are triangles, and the two sloping roof sides go down to the ground. Counting the floor, how many faces does the cabin have?
items.e: The cabin is a triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles (2 roof sides and the floor) = 5 faces.

items.q: Arjun sands every face of a wooden block shaped like an octagonal prism. How many faces does he sand?
items.e: 2 octagon ends + 8 rectangles = 10 faces. 9 would be an octagonal pyramid, and 16 is the number of vertices.

items.q: A hockey puck has 2 matching circle faces. Is it a prism?
c: No, it is a cylinder with a curved surface
Yes, it is a circular prism
items.e: A prism has only flat faces and polygon bases. A hockey puck has a curved surface, so it is a cylinder, not a prism.

items.q: Olivia’s pencil is a hexagonal prism. How many long flat faces run down its side (not counting the ends)?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 rectangles along the pencil. 8 counts the 2 ends as well, and 3 is how many you can see at once.

items.q: Ryan’s tent has a square floor and 4 triangle walls that meet at the top of one pole. What object is the tent shaped like?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at a point make a square pyramid.

items.q: On a camping trip on Vancouver Island, Ethan’s tent has 2 triangle ends, 2 sloping sides and a rectangle floor. What object is the tent shaped like?
items.e: 2 matching triangle ends joined by 3 rectangles (2 sides and the floor) make a triangular prism. Do not use its 5 faces to name it.

items.q: Emma builds a triangular prism and a square pyramid from toothpicks, with a marshmallow at every corner. How many marshmallows does she use in all?
items.e: Triangular prism: 6 vertices. Square pyramid: 4 + 1 apex = 5 vertices. 6 + 5 = 11. (17 counts the edges, 9 + 8.)

items.q: Liam stacks 10 matching hexagon tiles exactly on top of each other. What object does the stack look like?
items.e: Every layer is the same hexagon, so the top and bottom are matching hexagons joined by rectangles: a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Wei polishes every face of a glass paperweight shaped like a square pyramid. How many faces does he polish?
items.e: 1 square base + 4 triangles = 5 faces. 4 forgets the base, and 8 is the number of edges.

items.q: Leah builds a cedar planter box shaped like a rectangular prism with no top. How many wooden faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces. With no top, there are 6 − 1 = 5: the bottom and 4 sides.

items.q: Sofia builds the frame of a square pyramid with straws, one straw for each edge. How many straws does she need?
items.e: 4 straws round the square base + 4 up to the apex = 8. 5 is the number of faces (and of vertices).

items.q: In science class, a glass prism has 2 triangle ends. How many of its faces are rectangles?
items.e: A triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles, one rectangle for each side of the triangle.

items.q: Owen makes the frames of a pentagonal prism and a pentagonal pyramid from straws, one straw for each edge. How many straws altogether?
items.e: Prism: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 edges. Pyramid: 5 round the base + 5 up to the apex = 10. 15 + 10 = 25. (30 counts the prism twice, and 16 adds the vertices, 10 + 6.)

items.q: A chocolate box is a triangular prism. Each triangle end has 3 sides of 4 cm, and the box is 20 cm long. Harjot glues ribbon along every edge. How much ribbon is that?
items.e: Edges round the two ends: 6 × 4 = 24 cm. Three long edges: 3 × 20 = 60 cm. Total: 24 + 60 = 84 cm.

items.q: Ava’s tea bag is shaped like a pyramid with 4 faces, all triangles. What is its name?
items.e: 4 triangle faces: 1 triangle base and 3 triangles that meet at a point. That is a triangular pyramid.

items.q: A cereal box is a rectangular prism. Noah puts a sticker on every corner. How many stickers does he need?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 8 vertices: 4 on the top and 4 on the bottom. 6 is the number of faces and 12 the number of edges.

items.q: Hana builds a birdhouse. The front and back are shaped like a house (a square with a triangle roof on top) and are joined by rectangles. What object is the birdhouse?
items.e: The house shape has 5 sides, so the birdhouse is a pentagonal prism.
